 (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7928/2009  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Sri.Eeranna S/o late Thammanna, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 10.10.2009 at about 09.30 p.m, deceased Eeranna was crossing the road so as to reach the Attur Layout to visit house of Shivanna, at that time, the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-43-H-2827 came in high speed, in rash and negligent manner from South to North direction and dashed against the deceased.

Due to this the deceased sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Government hospital,
Yelahanka, wherein after first aid, he was referred to Victoria hospital for better treatment, but he was died on 11.10.2009 during the course of treatment.

03. It is further case of the petitioners that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as Mason and was skilled labour and (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 earning Rs.9,000/- p.m.
The petitioners were entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased.
After his death, petitioners don't have any other source of income for their livelihood due to the accident.
The petitioners have spent Rs.25,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
The accident in question occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
2 04.

entities.text: Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the initial stage, after registering the petition, notice were issued to the respondents, but the respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he is placed exparte and respondent No.1 Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

05. Respondent No.1 in its written statement denied all the material facts averred in the petition and also denied the alleged accident, rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle by its rider, age,
avocation, income of the deceased, dependency of the deceased (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 and also denied issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of offending Motor Cycle.
Further, it contended that its liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of insurance policy and also law governing thereto.
Further, it contended that alleged accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of the deceased as he was crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing.
Further, it is contended that the unknown vehicle might have hit the deceased while crossing the road.

Further, it is contended that for compensation sake, the insured vehicle has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident by giving false complaint against the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing reg. No.KA-43-H-2827.
Further, it is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and baseless.

On these grounds amongst other grounds,
respondent No.1 prayed for dismissal of the petition.
06. Earlier this case was disposed off by this tribunal by its Judgment dt:21.12.2010.

However, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company has preferred an Appeal against the Judgment and Award passed by this tribunal before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 in MFA No.1570/2015 c/w MFA Cross Objection No.108/2015 (MV-D), wherein para 8 of the said Judgment the Hon'ble High Court observed and held that, "When the Insurance Company has specifically denied the issuance of insurance policy, then it is the burden either on the claimants or respondent No.6- owner to prove the existence of insurance policy, because negative evidence cannot be proved by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, there is a disputed fact arises in this case as to whether there was existence of insurance policy or not.
This is the facts in issue to be proved before the tribunal.
But to this, the exercise in the trial before the tribunal was not made either of the parties.

Therefore, the matters are needed to be remanded to the tribunal for fresh consideration of the matters to find out as to whether there was insurance policy or not as on the date of time of accident as contended by the claimants and accordingly this case was remanded back to this tribunal for fresh disposal".
07.

After remanding the matter by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, though there is a specific direction to the parties to appear before the tribunal on (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 15.07.2024, but they have not appeared before the tribunal.

However, subsequently the petitioners have appeared before the tribunal and even despite service of notice to the respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle through paper publication which was duly published, but he remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Further, the respondents No.1 and 2 or the petitioners have not led any further evidence as per the directions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
Therefore, the earlier evidence led by the parties are already on record and same is required to be considered.

08. On the basis of the above said pleadings, following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:-
Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
3 01.

entities.text: Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners prove that on 10.10.2009 at about 9.30 p.m, deceased Eranna was crossing the road opposite to Mother Dairy Junction, near SFS 208,
Yelahanka New Town, Bangalore, at that time, the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-43-H-2827, came in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased Eeranna and thereby the said Eeranna sustained injuries and later on 11.10.09, succumbed to the injuries while taking treatment in Victoria hospital?
Whether petitioners prove that they are Legal representatives of deceased Eranna?
03. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so at what quantum and against whom, the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
04. What order?
09. To substantiate their case, the petitioners got examined petitioner No.1 as PW,1 and one witness as PW.2 and got marked documents Ex.P.1 to 8 and closed their side.
The respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence either before remanding the case or even after remanding the case.
10. I have heard the arguments and perused the records.

11. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7928/2009  REASONS 12. Issue No.1 & 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
4 14.

entities.text: Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW.2 is said to be eye-witness to the accident is also deposed about rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle by the rider and caused accident and he has seen the accident and he immediately shifted the injured to the Victoria hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was died while taking treatment on 11.10.2009.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of petitioners regarding rash and negligent (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 riding of Motor Cycle by the rider and death of deceased.
15.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 08 documents as Ex.P.1 to 8 on their behalf.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR and complaint registered U/Sec 279, 304(A) of IPC, Ex.P.2 is Spot panchanama, Ex.P.3 is Inquest report of deceased Eeranna, Ex.P.4 is Post mortem report of deceased Eeranna, wherein it is stated that the death is due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries sustained.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report which discloses involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

Ex.P.6 is Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle for rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle.

Ex.P.8 is Ration card of the family of the deceased and petitioners, which clearly goes to show that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 5 are the sons and petitioners No.3 and 4 are the daughters of the deceased Eeranna.

16. As already discussed above, the evidence of PW.1 with regard to Issue No.1 is corroborated with (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 the oral evidence of PW.2 who is admittedly eye- witness to the accident and who has also lodged complaint before the Police with regard to the accident in question.

17. Further, it is pertinent to note here that if really, accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself, the rider of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.2 ought to have come and contested the petitioner's case and he ought to have explained under what circumstances the accident is occurred and how he was not on fault.
Admittedly, respondent No.2 has remained exparte.
Further, respondent No.1 has also not led any contrary evidence to show that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased also.

Further, Police records and other evidence on record reveal that the accident occurred while crossing the road by the deceased and nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.2, who is eye-witness to the accident, that nearby the accident place there was a zebra cross for crossing the road and deceased and PW.2 were not used the said zebra cross for crossing the road.
The accident has taken place at about 9.30 p.m during night.
Normally (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 during night there will be no traffic in the road and people used to cross the road during night though there were no zebra crosses to cross the road.

Therefore, looking to the entire evidence available on record, it appears that the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by respondent No.2 and that there was no any contributory negligence on the part of deceased in occurrence of the accident in question and in the said accident itself, the deceased died due to injuries sustained by him and the petitioners have also proved that they are the legal representatives of the deceased Eeranna and PW.1 in her evidence deposed that she is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 5 are the sons and daughters of the deceased.
This fact has not been denied in the cross-examination.
Further, Ex.P.8 Ration card which discloses that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 5 are the sons and petitioners No.3 and 4 are the daughters of the deceased Eeranna.

Admittedly, the respondent No.1 has not lead Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
5 any evidence to show that the petitioners are not the legal representatives.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, considering the evidence, the petitioners have proved that accident (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 occurrred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle by its rider and deceased Eeranna was died in the road traffic accident and petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased Eeranna.
Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Eeranna, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

PW.1 who is the petitioner No.1 and wife of the deceased has stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 60 years and was working as Mason and was skilled labour and earning Rs.9,000/- p.m and petitioners have spent Rs.25,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
The petitioners were entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and after his demise, they don't have any other source of income for their livelihood due to the accident.
19. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The age of the deceased as per Police records (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 mentioned as 60 years and even in the petition also age of the deceased is mentioned as 60 years.

The petitioners have produced Ex.P.7 date of birth certificate of deceased said to have issued from one school situated in Andhra Pradesh, according to which the date of birth of deceased is 01.07.1957.
But said document does not bear any authorized round seal of the school and it is not in prescribed form.
So, the contents of Ex.P.7 cannot be believed.
Anyway looking to the evidence available on record, I hold that the deceased was aged about 60 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is 9.
20.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners in their petition as well as evidence stated that deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.9,000/- p.m.
Except oral evidence of PW.1, there is no other corroborated evidence to show that the deceased was earning Rs.9,000/- p.m.
In otherwords, so far as avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 produced any evidence or documents.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding avocation and income of deceased, this tribunal has placed reliance upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, the notional income as per the year 2009 is Rs.5,000/- per month.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
21.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In otherwords, there are 5 dependents and as per law, 1/4th of the income should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Since deceased was aged 60 years at the time of accident, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
6 income to be (5,000 + 500) = Rs.5,500/-.

entities.text:

6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (5,500 - 1,375) =
Rs.4,125/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.4,125/-.
As the deceased was aged about 60 years, the multiplier of 9 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.4,45,500/- (Rs.4,125/- x 12 x 9) towards loss of dependency.
22. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimants No.2 to 5 are major sons and daughters of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium as she lost her husband at an earliest.

Further, the petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of love and affection and they are entitled for Rs.18,000/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/4th of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Amount in  No. Compensation Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 4,45,500-00  (After deducting 1/4th of  the income towards  personal and living  expenses)
 2. Loss of spousal 48,000-00  consortium (petitioner  No.1)
 3. Loss of love and affection 1,60,000-00  (petitioners No.2 to 5)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 . Loss of estate 18,000-00  5. Funeral expenses and 18,000-00  transportation of
dead  body

Accordingly, I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,89,500/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
Regarding liability:-
As discussed earlier, this tribunal in its Judgment dt:21.12.2010 has allowed the petition and fasten the liability on the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Further, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company has challenged the said Judgment Rathnamma vs Nicl on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71726781/
7 before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.1570/2015 c/w MFA Cross Objection No.108/2015 (MV-D), wherein para 8 of the said Judgment dt:14.06.2024 the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that, "When the Insurance Company has specifically denied the issuance of insurance policy, then it is the burden either on the claimants or respondent No.6-owner to prove the existence of insurance policy, because negative evidence cannot be proved by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: Therefore, there is a disputed fact arises in this case as to whether there was existence of insurance policy or not.
This is the facts in issue to be proved before the tribunal.
But to this, the exercise in the trial before the tribunal was not made either of the parties.

Therefore, the matters are needed to be remanded to the tribunal for fresh consideration of the (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 matters to find out as to whether there was insurance policy or not as on the date of time of accident as contended by the claimants".
25.

Even after remanding the matter by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, either the claimants nor the respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle have not proved the existence of insurance policy and respondent No.2 remained absent and claimants have not lead any further evidence or produced copy of policy to prove existence of insurance policy.
Even on perusal of the claim petition of the petitioners, there is no mentioning any policy number in the claim petition.
There is no mention of type of policy allegedly issued by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that the respondent No.1 Insurance Company had issued a policy which is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.

On perusal of the records, it clearly goes to show that the respondent No.1 Insurance Company has not at all issued any policy in favour of the respondent No.2 owner with respect to the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the claimants and respondent No.2 are failed to prove that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of (SCCH-3)
20 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 the offending vehicle is in existence or is in force.

Therefore, under the above facts and circumstances of the case, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company is exonerated from payment of compensation since either the claimants nor the respondent No.2 owner has miserably failed to prove the existence of insurance policy allegedly issued by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, it is the respondent No.2 owner shall pay the above said compensation amount of Rs.6,89,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

26. Further, on behalf of the claimants, the following citations have been relied upon:-
01.

AIR 2018 SC 1900 in case of Mangla Ram V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.,
and others 02. AIR 2017 SC 5157 in case of National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others 03. 2018 ACJ 5 in case of Hem Raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., and others I have gone through the above citations and the same are taking into consideration while awarding compensation.

Further, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 5 are the major sons and daughters of the deceased Eeranna.,
Therefore, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.4,89,500/- and petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.50,000/- each in the award amount with accrued interest.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
28. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,89,500/- (Rupees Six lakhs eighty nine thousand and five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
(SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 The petition against respondent No.1 Insurance Company is hereby dismissed on without costs.
The petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.4,89,500/- and petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.50,000/- each in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one and the case is of the year 2009 more than 15 years old, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of petitioners through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petitioners were entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and after his demise, they don't have any other source of income for their livelihood due to the accident.
19. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
But said document does not bear any authorized round seal of the school and it is not in prescribed form.
Anyway looking to the evidence available on record, I hold that the deceased was aged about 60 years as on the date of accident.
As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is 9.
20.
Except oral evidence of PW.1, there is no other corroborated evidence to show that the deceased was earning Rs.9,000/- p.m.
Even after remanding the matter by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, either the claimants nor the respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle have not proved the existence of insurance policy and respondent No.2 remained absent and claimants have not lead any further evidence or produced copy of policy to prove existence of insurance policy.
Even on perusal of the claim petition of the petitioners, there is no mentioning any policy number in the claim petition.
There is no mention of type of policy allegedly issued by the Insurance Company.
Therefore, absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that the respondent No.1 Insurance Company had issued a policy which is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
On perusal of the records, it clearly goes to show that the respondent No.1 Insurance Company has not at all issued any policy in favour of the respondent No.2 owner with respect to the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the claimants and respondent No.2 are failed to prove that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of (SCCH-3)
20 M.V.C.No.7928/2009 the offending vehicle is in existence or is in force.
Therefore, under the above facts and circumstances of the case, the respondent No.1 Insurance Company is exonerated from payment of compensation since either the claimants nor the respondent No.2 owner has miserably failed to prove the existence of insurance policy allegedly issued by the Insurance Company.
